worst.problem: The skill makes the agent probe URLs while planning but never tells it to read robots.txt first, and gives it no way to check a URL against robots.txt. This contradicts POLICY.md's 'read first' rule, and in the Cursor trial the agent made the forbidden request to /dashboard. It is the only stumble where the skill led the agent to break its own published policy against a real site.
worst.where: skills/unreleased/references/plan.md (the 'Finding the URLs is in policy' paragraph); skills/unreleased/scripts/unreleased.py (subcommands)
worst.fix: In plan.md, make step 0 'Fetch https://<host>/robots.txt for each host you will probe (with the `ua` user agent) before any other request to that host; never probe a path under a Disallow line; list such a page in the plan instead (the engine records it as could-not-see).' Also add a small `unreleased.py robots <url>...` subcommand that reuses fetch.robots_rules/robots_disallows and prints allowed or disallowed for each URL. Then change plan.md's probe list to say 'check with `robots` first'.
worst.expected_effect: The blocking cursor-blocked-page stumble goes away: no disallowed request is made while planning, what the agent does matches POLICY.md (criterion 10 in substance), and the cursor-blocked-page eval ('could not see', 'robots.txt', '/dashboard') is reached without breaking policy.

fixer: Added an `unreleased.py robots <url>...` command that reads each host's robots.txt with the project user agent and prints allowed/disallowed per URL, and changed plan.md so planning first checks robots.txt, never probes a disallowed path, and lists such a page in the plan for the engine to record as could-not-see.
